To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Cnn scaffold assembles through an unusual 2:2 LZ:CM2 interaction, which forms an elongated, helical tetramer, that is required to form micron-scale assemblies in flies.
Cnn forms a scaffold at the mitotic centosome through an intrinsic ability to co-assemble into micron-scale complexes with itself.
Cnn assembles a mitotic centrosomal scaffold by forming a tetramer that can assemble into micron-scale structures that are required for mitotic assembly of centrosomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assembly of the mitotic centriole, which is a conserved organelle that nucleates microtubules and is essential for mitotic spindle formation.
the molecular mechanisms that control mitotic centrosomes, the major organelle of mitotic spindle formation.
understanding the assembly of the mitotic centriole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cnn scaffold is assembled by the formation of LZ:CM2 interactions between Cnn molecules that form a tetramer in vitro and a micron-scale assembly in vivo.
we solved the crystal structure of a 2: 2 LZ:CM2 interaction, which is required for centrosome assembly in flies.

We show that scaffold assembly of Centrosomin (a protein involved in centrosome assembly) requires conserved leuicne-zipper (LZ) domains that co-assembly into a 2-2 complex in vitro and that this complex is critical for mitotic-centrosome assembly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have solved the first crystal structure of the centrosome scaffold protein, Cnn, and that this structure reveals a novel mechanism by which Cnn assembles at the centrosome.
we have identified the structural basis for centrosome assembly in flies.
we identified a conserved leucin zipper and Cnn-moti 2 domain in Cnn that is required for mitotic assembly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assembly of a mitotic centrosomal scaffold is an intrinsically self-assembly process that is dependent on the assembly of a conserved leucin zipper domain and a Cnn-motiv 2 domain.
we identified a new mechanism of centrosome assembly that is conserved across species and that is mediated by a protein-protein interaction that is critical for centrosome assembly in vivo.
Cnn has an intrinsic ability to self-assemble into micron scale assemblies, and that this self-assembly is critical for centrosome assembly in flies.
